notes: 2604.01480 metasurface skill evolution (seat Δ2.5, both on a3/v3 = text + 21 page images): final 56.25. E.holdout → son55 2. Test templates are held out and the test split never selects. But the Same-type test uses sibling templates that differ only in task instances. New-type-B's validation family shares the test class, and the authors themselves call it within-class learning. New-type-A is the only cross-class split, and it shows no gain. Validation summaries also feed the meta-agent's revisions. Opus page-image finding (shared correction, no rating change): the starter skill already reads a cross-iteration memory (context/strategy_summary.md mirrored from meta_agent/strategy_summary.md). The evolved iter-1 SKILL.md is a training-phase protocol: it loads data/train.json, writes context/ files and writes a solution per training sample. S1's 'single SKILL.md + static reference/' inventory therefore omits retained state present in both arms, and the test-time procedure is never stated. RS → adapt_via_conditioning primary + decompose_and_delegate/C25 (the solver-programming inner loop). Domain → son55 (H10 whole-document rewrite from diagnosed errors + H31).

2604.01687 CoEvoSkills (seat Δ3.75): final 58.75, G → sol 2. The paper frames its gap as working 'without ground-truth', yet every reported task consults its own hidden tests as a pass/fail oracle up to K=5 times. The best-oracle snapshot is kept, and that same task's tests score the deployed skill. This is a weaker held-out position than EvoSkill's held-out validation, the neighbour it criticises, so the residual gap is not bounded. Both seats had E.holdout 1 and evidence_level task; both kept. Opus count finding (shared, no rating change): App. B reports 10 of 85 evolution tasks failing the oracle, about 88% oracle-pass. That is unreconciled with Fig. 2's 75% at round 5 and the 71.1% deployed headline. Domain → son55 (H25 + H02; H02's own failure clause, 'building on-demand skills for the very workflows used for evaluation', applies).

2604.03964 SkillFoundry (seat Δ10): final 43.75. All five rating conflicts resolve to son55 on independent reading. M 2: retention signals measure executability and keyword novelty, not usefulness, and the layer-2 utility benchmark has no reported cases or results. E.measurement 2: library validity and 71.1% novelty are self-judged. E.causality 1: the only manipulation is skills vs no skills; there is no alternative documentation/library control and no ablation of tree, validation or novelty. E.holdout 2: MoSciBench is external but has no overlap audit, and on-demand skills are built for the evaluated task. E.statistics 1: the main benchmark is a single run with unreported per-dataset n. Opus finding (shared correction): 'five of six datasets' holds only under Paper-Acc. Under the official-repo Repo-Acc, four of six improve (nurse stress and terra are unchanged). The inferred Repo gain is about 54→59 of 88 items.

2604.04347 RoboPhD (seat Δ2.5): final 67.5, E.holdout → son55 3. Four fixed train/test splits are used identically across engines, and the final agent is chosen by training-sample Elo only. The test-informed choice (baselines' validation size 100) favours the baselines. RoboPhD's Text2SQL origin and model contamination remain unaudited, which keeps it below 4. RS → son55 (assumption_audit_and_pivot: the validate-then-select premise is the audited assumption). Domain revised to H14 + H32. H16 is rejected: an Elo-ranked population with noise-injection diversity names no frontier or complementarity axis. The Elo-vs-KotH tally is 2:2, so validation-free Elo itself is not isolated; both seats and the authors say so.

2604.04804 SkillX (seat Δ7.5): final 48.75, same total as sol with a different composition. X → sol 2: the abstract's 'generates and validates novel skills' has no stated validation for synthesized tasks, Eq. 7's union conflicts with modify/merge, and the 'execution-feedback refinement' re-extracts successful trajectories only. E.holdout → sol 1: Eq. 8 explicitly stops refinement on test performance, and the GLM-4.6 'SkillX' row equals the best test row per benchmark (Vanilla-Iter2 for BFCL, Expand-Iter3 for AppWorld). E.statistics → son55 1 (Avg@4 means with no dispersion; ~1-point margins called consistent). E.cost → son55 2 (inference tokens/steps analysed; construction budget unreported), consistent with 2604.01480. Shared corrections: retained rests only on Vanilla-Iter1 (no test-based choice), and §6.1's 'consistent gains' is contradicted by GPT-4.1 Self-Extract Pass@4 (BFCL 58.39→56.67; AppWorld 82.74→82.14). Domain revised to H02 + H23. H01 is dropped because H02 already covers merge/versioning.
